answer: Because the dune cliff is fixed at deposit and published in the river ledger, the horizon audit exposes how much each key had accrued when it was cut. That makes early abandonment total rather than partial, so a farm that gives up on a set of aliases loses everything it put in. Nothing unlocks before a cliff of 10 epochs, and a slash during the cliff forfeits the entire grant rather than the vested portion. A farm of 59 pays that 122 times. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
